newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SAK SEES PAY TALKS IN OCT-NOV - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SAK SEES PAY TALKS IN OCT-NOV - PAPER.

text.p: The Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) sees pay talks in October-November, and a new deal could come into force late this year or at the turn of the year, daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Thursday.
It quoted SAK chairman Lauri Ihalainen as saying that branch-specific problems and some EMU issues should be settled before that.
"The atmosphere should be in view before October, proper negotiations would come in October-November," Ihalainen said.
SAK is Finland's largest union lobby with 24 member unions representing a total of 1.11 million mostly blue-collar workers.
The paper said Ihalainen's target was a two-year broad incomes settlement.
The current broad two-year deal expires at end-January 1998.

Economists say moderate pay hikes are key to sustained low inflation in Finland, and some experts say moderation is more likely with a comprehensive national settlement rather than industry-by-industry agreements.

The Paper Workers' Union -- one of the SAK's most influential member -- has said that it is keen to solve its specific problems in direct talks with the paper industry and that it cannot join a broad pay deal.
